The **2022 FIA Formula One World Championship** was a motor racing championship for [Formula One cars](Formula_One_cars "Formula One cars"), which was the 73rd running of the [Formula One World Championship](Formula_One_World_Championship "Formula One World Championship").[[lower-alpha 1]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-1) It is recognised by the [Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile](F%C3%A9d%C3%A9ration_Internationale_de_l'Automobile "Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile") (FIA), the governing body of international [motorsport](Motorsport "Motorsport"), as the highest class of competition for [open-wheel racing cars](Open-wheel_car "Open-wheel car"). The championship was contested over twenty-two [Grands Prix](Formula_One#Grands_Prix "Formula One"), which were held around the world, and ended earlier than in recent years to avoid overlapping with the [FIFA World Cup](2022_FIFA_World_Cup "2022 FIFA World Cup").[[1]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-Reuters_F1_calendar-2)[[2]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-BBC_Sport_2022_calendar-3)

Drivers and teams competed for the titles of [World Drivers' Champion](List_of_Formula_One_World_Drivers'_Champions "List of Formula One World Drivers' Champions") and [World Constructors' Champion](List_of_Formula_One_World_Constructors'_Champions "List of Formula One World Constructors' Champions"), respectively. The 2022 championship saw the introduction of significant changes to the sport's technical regulations. These changes had been intended to be introduced in [2021](2021_Formula_One_World_Championship "2021 Formula One World Championship"), but were delayed until 2022 [in response](Impact_of_the_COVID-19_pandemic_on_motorsport "Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on motorsport") to the [COVID-19 pandemic](COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[3]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-19_chassis-4) [Max Verstappen](Max_Verstappen "Max Verstappen"), who was the reigning Drivers' Champion, claimed his second title at the [Japanese Grand Prix](2022_Japanese_Grand_Prix "2022 Japanese Grand Prix"), while his team, [Red Bull Racing](Red_Bull_Racing "Red Bull Racing"), achieved their fifth World Constructor Championship, and first since [2013](2013_Formula_One_World_Championship "2013 Formula One World Championship"), at the following [United States Grand Prix](2022_United_States_Grand_Prix "2022 United States Grand Prix"). [Mercedes](Mercedes-Benz_in_Formula_One "Mercedes-Benz in Formula One") were the reigning Constructors' Champion.[[4]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-5)[[5]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-6)[[6]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-7)

This was the final season for four-time World Champion [Sebastian Vettel](Sebastian_Vettel "Sebastian Vettel").[[7]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-8) Seven-time World Champion [Lewis Hamilton](Lewis_Hamilton "Lewis Hamilton") endured a difficult season with [Mercedes](Mercedes-Benz_in_Formula_One "Mercedes-Benz in Formula One"), failing to secure either a pole position or Grand Prix win during the season, the first time either occurrence had happened in his Formula One career since it began in [2007](2007_Formula_One_World_Championship "2007 Formula One World Championship").[[8]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-9)[[9]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-10)

### Team changes

[Honda](Honda_in_Formula_One "Honda in Formula One") initially stated that they would not supply power units beyond [2021](2021_Formula_One_World_Championship "2021 Formula One World Championship").[[36]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-42) The company had provided power units to [Scuderia AlphaTauri](Scuderia_AlphaTauri "Scuderia AlphaTauri") (previously called [Scuderia Toro Rosso](Scuderia_Toro_Rosso "Scuderia Toro Rosso")) since [2018](2018_Formula_One_World_Championship "2018 Formula One World Championship") and to [Red Bull Racing](Red_Bull_Racing "Red Bull Racing") since [2019](2019_Formula_One_World_Championship "2019 Formula One World Championship").[[37]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-AlphaTauri-43) Initially, Red Bull Racing planned to take over Honda's engine programme and manage it in-house, under a new division called [Red Bull Powertrains](Red_Bull_Powertrains "Red Bull Powertrains"). The decision was made after lobbying the other nine teams to negotiate an engine development freeze until 2025. Red Bull Racing acknowledged that they would have left the championship if the engine development freeze had not been agreed to as they could not develop a brand new engine, and both Red Bull Racing and [Renault](Renault_in_Formula_One "Renault in Formula One") were unwilling to resume their former partnership.[[27]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-RedBull-engine-29)[[38]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-44)[[lower-alpha 7]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-46) Honda later agreed to continue supplying Red Bull Racing and AlphaTauri for [2023](2023_Formula_One_World_Championship "2023 Formula One World Championship") with engines for this season, which were rebadged to Red Bull Powertrains.[[40]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-47) In addition to the assembly and maintenance of the engines, Honda continued to provide Red Bull Racing and AlphaTauri with technical and operational oversight during race weekends.[[41]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-48)

### Driver changes

[Zhou Guanyu](Zhou_Guanyu "Zhou Guanyu") (left) made his Formula One debut driving for [Alfa Romeo](Alfa_Romeo_in_Formula_One "Alfa Romeo in Formula One"). [Nikita Mazepin](Nikita_Mazepin "Nikita Mazepin") (centre), who was originally going to compete for [Haas](Haas_F1_Team "Haas F1 Team"), had his contract terminated amidst the [Russian invasion of Ukraine](2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine"). Mazepin was subsequently replaced by [Kevin Magnussen](Kevin_Magnussen "Kevin Magnussen") (right).

[Fernando Alonso](Fernando_Alonso "Fernando Alonso") (left) broke [Kimi Räikkönen](Kimi_R%C3%A4ikk%C3%B6nen "Kimi Räikkönen")'s (right) record for the most race starts and race entries at the [Singapore](2022_Singapore_Grand_Prix "2022 Singapore Grand Prix") and [Japanese](2022_Japanese_Grand_Prix "2022 Japanese Grand Prix") Grands Prix, respectively.

[Kimi Räikkönen](Kimi_R%C3%A4ikk%C3%B6nen "Kimi Räikkönen") retired following the conclusion of the 2021 championship; Räikkönen won 21 races, and the [2007 World Drivers' Championship](2007_Formula_One_World_Championship "2007 Formula One World Championship") across a 19 season Formula career.[[42]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-49) Räikkönen's seat at [Alfa Romeo](Alfa_Romeo_in_Formula_One "Alfa Romeo in Formula One") was filled by [Valtteri Bottas](Valtteri_Bottas "Valtteri Bottas"), who left [Mercedes](Mercedes-Benz_in_Formula_One "Mercedes-Benz in Formula One") after 5 seasons.[[43]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-50) [George Russell](George_Russell_(racing_driver) "George Russell (racing driver)") replaced Bottas,[[44]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-51)[[45]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-:2-52) vacating the seat that he had held for the past 3 seasons at [Williams](Williams_Grand_Prix_Engineering "Williams Grand Prix Engineering"). Russell was replaced by former [Red Bull Racing](Red_Bull_Racing "Red Bull Racing") driver [Alex Albon](Alex_Albon "Alex Albon").[[46]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-53)

[Zhou Guanyu](Zhou_Guanyu "Zhou Guanyu"), who finished third in the [2021 Formula 2 Championship](2021_Formula_2_Championship "2021 Formula 2 Championship"), joined Alfa Romeo, in place of [Antonio Giovinazzi](Antonio_Giovinazzi "Antonio Giovinazzi"), who had been at the team since 2019.[[47]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-Zhou-54)[[48]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-55) Zhou became the first Chinese driver to compete in Formula One.[[47]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-Zhou-54)

[Nikita Mazepin](Nikita_Mazepin "Nikita Mazepin") was originally contracted to compete for [Haas](Haas_F1_Team "Haas F1 Team"), as part of a multi-year contract that started in 2021. Following the [Russian invasion of Ukraine](2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine") and the resultant cancellation of <Uralkali>'s title sponsorship of Haas, his contract was terminated.[[49]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-56) He was replaced by [Kevin Magnussen](Kevin_Magnussen "Kevin Magnussen"), who had last competed in [2020](2020_Formula_One_World_Championship "2020 Formula One World Championship") with the same team.[[50]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-57)

He was replaced at [Williams](Williams_Grand_Prix_Engineering "Williams Grand Prix Engineering") by the [Mercedes](Mercedes-Benz_in_Formula_One "Mercedes-Benz in Formula One") reserve driver [2020–21 Formula E](2020%E2%80%9321_Formula_E_World_Championship "2020–21 Formula E World Championship") and [2019 Formula 2](2019_Formula_2_Championship "2019 Formula 2 Championship") Champion [Nyck de Vries](Nyck_de_Vries "Nyck de Vries"), who made his Formula One race debut.[[53]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-60)

Following the race, a conspiracy theory emerged accusing Red Bull Racing strategist Hannah Schmitz of conspiring with sister team AlphaTauri to ensure a favourable result for Verstappen, after questioning the nature of Tsunoda's retirement. The incident was looked into by race stewards, whose only action was to reprimand Tsunoda for having undone his belts on track.[[185]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-:02-193)[[186]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-Tsunoda-194)

Leclerc took pole at the [Italian Grand Prix](2022_Italian_Grand_Prix "2022 Italian Grand Prix") with Verstappen taking second. He, alongside Sainz and Hamilton, took penalties for replacing components.[[187]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-195) Verstappen started from seventh, but reached second by lap 5, behind Leclerc who had held successfully defended first position. After Vettel experienced an engine failure on lap 10,[[188]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-amitaly-196) Leclerc pitted under the virtual safety car.[[189]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-msitaly-197) Verstappen would then lead the race until he pitted on lap 26.[[190]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-198) Alonso's Alpine would then be retired because of a water pressure issue on lap 31, but was returned to the pit lane to avoid any disruptions to the race.[[191]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-199) Leclerc made a second pit stop on lap 34, again giving Verstappen the lead. Stroll retired on lap 39 and on lap 47, Ricciardo stopped his car on the side of the track and a safety car was deployed.[[188]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-amitaly-196)[[189]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-msitaly-197) Verstappen held the position and won under the safety car.[[189]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-msitaly-197)

### Closing rounds

The [Singapore Grand Prix](2022_Singapore_Grand_Prix "2022 Singapore Grand Prix") was the first race wherein Verstappen could win the championship mathematically, needing to outscore Leclerc by 22 points, Pérez by 13 and George Russell by 6. If Verstappen came first with the fastest lap while Leclerc came eighth or lower and Pérez came fourth or lower, or if Verstappen came first without the fastest lap while Leclerc came ninth or lower and Pérez came either fourth without the fastest lap or fifth with, Verstappen would be the champion.[[192]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-200) Leclerc was on pole after Verstappen abandoned two qualifying laps, the first due to traffic, and the second to ensure there would be enough fuel for the governing body to take a sample at the end of the session, thus avoiding a disqualification from the qualifying session. Verstappen started in eighth.[[193]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-201) The race was delayed by over an hour due to thunderstorms.[[194]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-202) Pérez won the race, followed by Leclerc and Sainz. Verstappen came seventh.[[195]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-203)

Following Verstappen's failure to secure the championship at the Singapore Grand Prix, several permutations could net him the championship at the following [Japanese Grand Prix](2022_Japanese_Grand_Prix "2022 Japanese Grand Prix"). He needed to outscore Leclerc by eight points and Pérez by six.[[196]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-204) Verstappen would secure pole, in front of Leclerc, Sainz, and Pérez. The race began on time despite poor weather and was red-flagged after two laps following an accident involving Sainz. The deployment of the recovery vehicle during the red flag was criticised; Gasly narrowly missed it in poor weather conditions. Gasly angrily remonstrated that "[he] could have killed [himself]" if he had lost control and hit the vehicle, even at reduced speed.[[197]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-205) The race resumed at 16:15 local time behind the safety car. Only twenty-eight laps were completed before the race was curtailed due to it passing the three-hour time limit. Verstappen won by just under 27 seconds, with Leclerc coming second and Pérez coming third. After an investigation involving the latter two in the final lap, Leclerc was handed a five-second penalty, meaning he came third behind Pérez.[[198]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-206) As the race was completed, full points were awarded despite the confusion that only partial points were on offer due to the reduced total length of the race. Verstappen was crowned World Champion, having an insurmountable lead of 113 points, with only 112 still available.[[199]](2022_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-207)

With the Drivers' Championship secured, Red Bull Racing set about securing their first Constructors' Championship since [2013](2013_Formula_One_World_Championship "2013 Formula One World Championship"), which they did by outscoring Ferrari by twenty-two points at the [United States Grand Prix](2022_United_States_Grand_Prix "2022 United States Grand Prix"). Sainz took his third pole position of the season, and was spun by [George Russell](George_Russell_(racing_driver) "George Russell (racing driver)") into turn one and forced to retire due to the resulting damage. Mercedes had a chance at winning after [Lewis Hamilton](Lewis_Hamilton "Lewis Hamilton") took the lead through a very slow pit stop for Verstappen. Verstappen overturned a four-second gap to retake the lead on lap 50. This race was notable for a collision between [Fernando Alonso](Fernando_Alonso "Fernando Alonso") and [Lance Stroll](Lance_Stroll "Lance Stroll"), which sent Alonso airborne. Alonso continued and finished the race in seventh, only to receive a thirty-second penalty post-race after [Haas](Haas_F1_Team "Haas F1 Team") protested the decision not to show Alonso a black and orange flag due to his right wing mirror dislodging during the race. This penalty was overturned four days later, as the FIA determined that Haas did not submit their protest within thirty minutes of the race finishing, making the protest inadmissible.

Verstappen took his sixth pole position and his fourteenth race win of the season at the [Mexico City Grand Prix](2022_Mexico_City_Grand_Prix "2022 Mexico City Grand Prix"), breaking the record for most wins in a Formula One season, previously held jointly by [Michael Schumacher](Michael_Schumacher "Michael Schumacher") ([2004](2004_Formula_One_World_Championship "2004 Formula One World Championship")) and [Sebastian Vettel](Sebastian_Vettel "Sebastian Vettel") ([2013](2013_Formula_One_World_Championship "2013 Formula One World Championship")). [Daniel Ricciardo](Daniel_Ricciardo "Daniel Ricciardo") made his way from thirteenth to seventh in sixteen laps while also dealing with a ten-second time penalty due to a collision with [Yuki Tsunoda](Yuki_Tsunoda "Yuki Tsunoda").

The [São Paulo Grand Prix](2022_S%C3%A3o_Paulo_Grand_Prix "2022 São Paulo Grand Prix") was the third and final sprint weekend of the season, meaning qualifying was on Friday, in wet conditions. [Kevin Magnussen](Kevin_Magnussen "Kevin Magnussen") took the first pole position of his Formula One career, as well as Haas' first. Magnussen was unable to keep the faster cars at bay during the sprint, and Mercedes were able to lock out the front row for the Grand Prix on Sunday, which they converted into their first one-two finish since the [2020 Emilia Romagna Grand Prix](2020_Emilia_Romagna_Grand_Prix "2020 Emilia Romagna Grand Prix"), with Russell taking his first win in Formula One. The race involved collisions between Magnussen and Ricciardo, Verstappen and Hamilton and, Norris and Leclerc. At the conclusion of the race, Verstappen rejected a team order to let teammate Pérez pass him for sixth place, stating that he told the team in the summer to not give Pérez any preferential team orders.

Verstappen took a seventh pole position at the season ending [Abu Dhabi Grand Prix](2022_Abu_Dhabi_Grand_Prix "2022 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix") and a fifteenth win on the season, extending the record that he had set in Mexico City. Charles Leclerc held off a faster Sergio Pérez to claim second place, earning Leclerc second in the Drivers' Championship as well. Two Constructors' Championship places came down to the final race of the season; Mercedes was unable to pass Ferrari for second after Russell finished fifth and Hamilton retired with a gearbox failure, while [Aston Martin](Aston_Martin_in_Formula_One "Aston Martin in Formula One") and [Alfa Romeo](Alfa_Romeo_in_Formula_One "Alfa Romeo in Formula One") finished tied on points, with Alfa Romeo claiming sixth on countback. The race was the final one for [Sebastian Vettel](Sebastian_Vettel "Sebastian Vettel"), who retired, and for [Nicholas Latifi](Nicholas_Latifi "Nicholas Latifi") and [Mick Schumacher](Mick_Schumacher "Mick Schumacher"), who were unable to secure a race seat for 2023.
